claims.original_claim: Baseline là bản phát triển từ Piper, không phải Piper nguyên bản hay bản tái tạo đầy đủ VITS2.
claims.original_claim_en: The baseline is a development of Piper, neither the original Piper nor a complete VITS2 reproduction.
claims.proposed_narrowed_claim: The selected baseline checkpoint (epoch 1489) and the model built from the released hifi-mobiNet code expose the same 876 parameter/buffer names (876/876). The published Piper lj-medium checkpoint exposes 784 names; the baseline additionally holds 72 flow-attention and 20 duration-discriminator names that the Piper checkpoint lacks. This is a name-level structural comparison.
claims.author_account: Author statement (2026-10-05/07): the baseline was rewritten following Piper's design and combines selected VITS2 components; Piper was not forked or cloned. Recorded as the author's account, not as evidence derived from artifacts.
claims.pc_reported_assessment: Supportable in narrowed form (PC README 2026-10-07: 'Hỗ trợ được (bản thu hẹp)').
claims.comparison_basis: parameter and persistent-buffer NAMES only; tensor shapes, values, forward behaviour, executed source code and code origin are not compared

comparator_inventories.baseline_checkpoint_vs_code_edgetts_use_: 876 vs 881, 876 common; only in EdgeTTS code: ['model_g.enc_q.enc._n_channels', 'model_g.flow.flows.0.enc._n_channels', 'model_g.flow.flows.2.enc._n_channels', 'model_g.flow.flows.4.enc._n_channels', 'model_g.flow.flows.6.enc._n_channels']
comparator_inventories.piper_checkpoint_vs_code_edgetts_config_: 784 vs 789, 784 common (EdgeTTS Config A used as the Piper-base comparator; upstream Piper code was not built)
comparator_inventories.baseline_checkpoint_vs_piper_checkpoint: 92 names only in baseline (= 72 'model_g.flow.*.attn.*' + 20 'model_d_dur.*'), 0 only in Piper

evidence.availability: workstation; team checkpoints in the private HF archive; Piper public

limitations: Equal names show structural compatibility of the stored state, not identical forward computation, not which code was executed, and not code lineage.
Code-side inventories come from the current checkout (relocated BanhmiTTS code and vendored EdgeTTS a73a897), not from code archived at training time.

The 5 '_n_channels' buffers produced by current EdgeTTS code are absent from the checkpoint; this shows a difference from current EdgeTTS code only and is not used to infer which code trained the baseline.
Differences from VITS2 (linear-spectrogram posterior input, blank tokens kept) come from code/config reading and the VITS2 paper, not from this name comparison.
remaining_inputs: Training-time source snapshot or commit tied to the checkpoint run, if a code-origin statement is wanted.
Shape-level comparison (possible without unpickling only with a dedicated reader; not done here).

claims.original_claim: ONNX FP32 cuối được export từ đúng checkpoint và đạt parity với PyTorch.
claims.original_claim_en: The final FP32 ONNX graphs were exported from the intended checkpoints and match PyTorch.
claims.proposed_narrowed_claim: Each of the four Q05 FP32 graphs (published at DazielNguyen/hifi-mobiNet-inference revision f760e85a) carries in its metadata the SHA-256 of the checkpoint recorded for that run, and on 10 stored parity cases per model the ONNX output matched PyTorch within thresholds declared in the run configuration before the runs (NRMSE <= 1e-3, max |error| <= 5e-3).
claims.pc_reported_assessment: Supported for the Q05 graphs (PC README: 'Hỗ trợ (cho graph Q05)').

nrmse.formula: err = pytorch - onnx; nrmse = sqrt(mean(err^2)) / max(sqrt(mean(pytorch^2)), 1e-12); pass = same shape AND finite AND nrmse <= 0.001 AND max|err| <= 0.005; aggregate = all 10 cases pass (max reported)
nrmse.aggregation: all cases must pass; maximum and mean over cases reported
nrmse.prespecified_proof: RUN_CONFIG.json created_utc 2026-10-04T00:08:30Z declares thresholds_declared_before_runs; the first model run started 00:09:02Z (REPORT.*.started_utc); the runner asserts the config thresholds. An earlier directory (00:07:44Z) holds the same thresholds.

graph_identity_notes: Validation graphs (external noise inputs) and deployed graphs have identical initializers (422/478/454/382) and differ only in 2 RandomNormalLike nodes: identical initializers, not an identical pipeline.

A matching metadata checkpoint hash records what the exporter was told; it does not by itself prove which checkpoint bytes were read at export time. The Q05 runner computed the SHA-256 of the snapshot it loaded (strict load) in the same run.
limitations: 10 inputs per model, ONNX Runtime 1.23.2 CPU, 2 threads; parity under the validation graphs with injected noise.
Says nothing about the historical benchmark or INT8 graphs (see J-C023/J-C024).

claims.original_claim: SEQ có chất lượng tương đương Parallel-IR.
claims.original_claim_en: SEQ has quality equivalent to Parallel-IR (MRF).
claims.proposed_narrowed_claim: Equivalence was not established: no equivalence margin or test was pre-specified. On Harvard-720 the data describe a runtime-quality trade-off: SEQ minus MRF WER = +0.0149 (fraction of words; paired bootstrap 95% CI [+0.0019, +0.0277], i.e. +0.19 to +2.77 percentage points; Wilcoxon p = 0.052, Holm-adjusted 0.094), UTMOSv2 difference -0.024 (CI [-0.046, -0.001]), with 9.1% lower mean RTF for SEQ.
claims.pc_reported_assessment: PC README labels this 'Bị dữ liệu phản bác ở WER' (contradicted on WER). Not adopted: a CI excluding 0 is not an equivalence test.

wer.scale: fraction of words, macro mean over 720 utterances

values.interpretation_limit: a CI that excludes 0 is not an equivalence test; no equivalence margin was declared

method.bootstrap: paired, 10,000 resamples of the 720 per-sentence differences, percentile 2.5/97.5, numpy default_rng(20261004) shared across the 15 tests in order

limitations: One synthesis draw, one scorer pass and one training run per model; exploratory statistics.
Not labelled CONTRADICTED: no equivalence design exists to contradict.
remaining_inputs: A pre-specified equivalence margin with a matching test (e.g. TOST), if an equivalence claim is wanted.

claims.original_claim_en: SEQ's speed advantage holds across PyTorch, ONNX FP32 and INT8.
claims.proposed_narrowed_claim: In historical ONNX Runtime CPU runs on the same 500 LJSpeech sentences, SEQ was faster than the ResBlock2 baseline on 495/500 sentences in FP32 (median RTF ratio 0.89) and 498/500 after backbone PTQ (0.84). These are SEQ-vs-baseline results; no identified MRF graph was benchmarked under the same conditions.
claims.pc_reported_assessment: Partly supported, SEQ vs baseline (PC README: 'Hỗ trợ một phần').

claims.original_claim: Toàn bộ mô tả flow, số tham số và phạm vi node /flow/ trong PTQ đều đúng với model liên quan.
claims.original_claim_en: The flow description, its parameter count and the /flow/ node scope in PTQ are all correct for the models concerned.
claims.proposed_narrowed_claim: In the Q05 FP32 graphs the flow of baseline, MRF and SEQ holds 8,285,568 initializer elements (weights and biases) and contains 64 Conv, 16 MatMul, 4 Softmax and 8 LayerNormalization nodes; Piper's flow holds 7,090,560 after removing weight-norm gains, with 40 Conv and no attention ops. Separately, the historical PTQ quantized all 64 flow convolutions, and the flow attention MatMuls only in SEQ.
claims.pc_reported_assessment: Supported in narrowed, artifact-specific form (PC README: 'Hỗ trợ (thu hẹp về artifact cụ thể)').
claims.counting_method: Sum of elements of the unique initializers consumed by nodes named /flow/* or whose name starts with 'flow.'; includes weights and biases (bias elements reported separately); no initializer is shared with non-flow nodes; for Piper the weight_g tensors are subtracted (weight norm not folded in its export). Constant-node tensors inside /flow/ (754 elements internal, 176 Piper) are not counted. Buffers are not initializers unless exported as such.
interpretation_limits: Op counts identify graph operators, not module types: 4 Softmax nodes show 4 attention softmaxes in the exported flow, not the number of heads or layer design.
The architecture description (what the flow is) and the PTQ /flow/ scope (which flow nodes were quantized in historical graphs) are separate statements; see J-C024 for the latter.
